candidates.name: Traumatic maculopathy
support_spans: central macular thickening in fundus examination
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption in the right eye
contradict_spans: Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities in either eye
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with traumatic maculopathy, a condition that can occur after blunt trauma to the eye.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve protection because it is a rare and easily missed cause of vision loss after trauma.

candidates.name: Photoreceptor damage from lightning strike
support_spans: subtle irregularity of the outer retinal layers, most notable nasal to the fovea
further loss of outer retinal layers in the nasal macula
contradict_spans: Preserved foveal contour in both eyes without cystoid abnormalities
candidates.why: The lightning strike may have caused direct damage to the photoreceptors, leading to outer retinal layer loss and vision loss.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may deserve protection because it is a rare and specific cause of vision loss after a lightning strike.
